native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Considering academic characteristics (ASVAB achievement, class-rank percentile, baseline schooling) substantially attenuates the effects of SES and race on BA-track college attendance (the available proxy for BA completion in nls_raw.csv): the SES odds ratio falls from 2.29 to 1.67 (~38% attenuation in log-odds; ~41% in the linear model), the raw Black disadvantage is eliminated (OR 0.70→0.86; sign reversal in the LPM), and the Hispanic pattern reverses to the highest net-of-achievement attendance (OR 2.86) once their much lower measured ASVAB scores (likely language-related measurement bias) are accounted for. Academic characteristics themselves dominate prediction (OR≈2.1 per SD ASVAB; OR≈4.3 for class-rank percentile), indicating that academic skills are the principal channel through which SES and race relate to BA-track college attendance.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Built dorm-residence-based college-attendance outcome (type 3 in any 1981-1996 wave; prevalence 9.4% overall / 16.2% analytic); 2) standardized SES composite (mother+father education, log 1979 income, topcode winsorized); 3) academic set = re-standardized 4-subtest ASVAB composite, class-rank percentile (1-rank/classsize), HGC 1979; 4) nested logit + LPM (M0 race+SES, M1 +academics, M2 +interactions) on complete cases n=5,095 with fixed sex/age controls; 5) attenuation measured M0→M1 on identical sample; 6) sensitivities: +log wealth 1985 (n=4,565) and missing-indicator imputation (N=12,686). Outputs: analysis.py, outputs/analysis_log.txt, outputs/results.json, outputs/summary.md.
